media.alt: AKU provides eighty fellows, residents and interns to serve the nation

content.text: "AKU is improving standards of postgraduate medical training in Pakistan and some of its graduates are in key positions on the Faculty of the College of Physicians and Surgeons", said Professor Sultan M. Farooqui, President. College of Physicians and Surgeons of Pakistan (CPSP). Professor Sultan was the chief guest at the Graduation Ceremony for fellows, residents and interns organized by the Department of Postgraduate Medical Education (PGME) of TIle Aga Khan University (AKU) on October 23.1999.

The Department of Postgraduate Medical Education has introduced a core curriculum for trainees that stresses not only clinical skills. but also emphasizes instruction in ethics. communication skills and computer literacy. Dr Farhat Moazam, Associate Dean, PGME, emphasized that AKU was committed to producing humane and ethical generalists and specialists for this country. who combine clinical expertise with wisdom and compassion.

Dr Shamsh Kassim-Lakha. S.I., President, AKU, distributed certificates to 43 residents for completion of training in the 16 disciplines, which are approved by CPSP. In addition, those in General Surgery. Orthopedics, Internal Medicine. Obs/Gyn and Family Medicine are also recognized by the relevant Royal Colleges in tile U'K.

Dr Camer Vellani. Rector. AKU. awarded certificates to 44 interns. Dr Shahryar Noordin was the recipient of the Best Intern Award for 1999. This was followed by Dr Kashif, who presented the valicditory speech as the representative of the graduating residents. Finally. Professor Farooqui awarded two fellowships in Adult Cardiology and Gastroenterology.

Since 1986, AKU has graduated 2~2 young men and women from its postgraduate programmes. Among those trained to date. almost 40 percent come from outside Karachi. Following graduation. the majority have continued to work in Pakistan and many are on the AKU faculty having risen to senior ranks in several departments. Even more heartening is the fact that many others are on the staff and faculty of reputable teaching institutions throughout the country. Thus. these residency programmes are providing the nation with an important reserve of skilled specialists.

This success in training generalists and specialists, oyer a relatively short time. confirms that colleges and universities in the private sector can play a significant role in improving medical postgraduate education and training in Pakistan.
